column1: # Every XGIMI remote and remote-like input device known from the stock dumps (README.md: evidence and rules).
# One row per device. Read by tools/remotes/gen_catalog.py, which writes apps/core/lumen-remote/src/org/lumen/remote/RemoteCatalog.java
# (never edit that file by hand: edit this table and run the generator; --check is a test).
#  id        stable name used in code, art and logs
#  kind      ble_remote (paired over Bluetooth LE by lumen-remote), ble_music (XGIMI music controller, paired like a remote),
#            usb_dongle (2.4 GHz remote with its own USB receiver, nothing to pair), ir (the projector's IR receiver),
#            keypad (the projector's own keys), generic (vendor reference layout of a non XGIMI device)
#  names     advertised Bluetooth names, '|' separated; a name matches when the advertised name contains it, case-sensitive,
#            as the stock RcPair rule (BluRemConService.isXgimiRc: String.contains)
#  vid_pid   HID vendor:product as the input device reports it (the key layout file Vendor_<vid>_Product_<pid>.kl)
#  input     input device name seen on a unit ('-' = not seen live)
#  combo     keys held to put the remote into pairing mode (HOME+BACK = Home and Back together until the light blinks)
#  voice     mic path: hid_audio (voice over the HID audio report, vendor remote.txt), - none
#  battery   gatt_bas (Battery Service 0x180F / 0x2A19, read by stock XgimiRcInfo), - none
#  art       picture the pairing screens draw (lumen-remote res: lumen_remote_<art>*.xml)
#  stock     stock models whose vendor ships this layout file (vendor/usr/keylayout), G code list
#  lumen_kl  1 = every Lumen image must carry a Lumen copy in /system/product/usr/keylayout (the stock file uses labels
#            Lineage cannot parse, so without our copy the device falls back to Generic.kl)
#  evidence  where the row comes from
